_comment: Hand corrections to the reader's output for A14, in pixels of the
full-resolution crops in .build/a14/ (see imageSize / sheetImageSize).
The reader did well on this board -- 140 of 177 located, 79%, against A17's
47% -- because A14's silkscreen stands clear of the component outlines. Every
marker was still reviewed by eye, tier by tier, and the error rate is very
uneven across the tiers:
agreed     99 of 101 right   (C4 landed on 'P612', C5 on the 'ASSY' silkscreen)
ambiguous   8 of 14 right
single      8 of 9 right
collision   8 of 16 right
which is the same shape as A17: agreed is the best tier and still not a clean
one, and collision is a coin toss. The 17 wrong ones are replaced by hand below
rather than dropped, since every one of them is legible on the drawing.
R1 to R5 were misread as a group -- R1 onto the 'ROL' of the CONTROL
silkscreen, R2 onto CR2, R3 onto R30, R4 onto CR4, R5 onto R37. Four of the
five are the carbon composition parts that changed stock number between
revisions, which is a coincidence, but it is worth knowing that the whole
R1-R5 group is hand placed.
All six test points are placed by hand. Each is drawn as a short vertical bar
with its label immediately to the right, and the labels sit in a row about 80 px
apart, so a marker wide enough to cover pad and label will reach the neighbour
unless it is placed deliberately: the box is narrowed to 100 px and centred so
the pad falls on its left edge.
Sheet 4 carries no circuit -- it is the relay state table -- so no OCR pass is
run against it and nothing is placed on it.
32 board entries carry "fitted": true. Those are the component body rather
than the designator that names it, measured off the drawing by
tools/detect_round_parts.py and then rendered and looked at one by one:
fifteen relays, six DIP and two flat-pack ICs, the CR5 bridge, the J1
header, seven cans and U3's TO-5. The build treats them like any other
hand-placed entry; the flag only records how the numbers were arrived at.
K9 is the one relay declined -- its designator is printed outside the
outline. The tantalums C6, C7 and C11 are fitted despite being drawn as
broken arcs, and sit at 69-78% ray agreement against 97-100% for the
relays; they were checked with more care for that reason and are right.

_schematicComment: Hand placements for parts the reader left with no schematic position at all.
Each was found by cropping the sheet at full resolution and reading the label,
and the box is the printed designator, centre, in pixels of schN_full.png.
Most of them had a reader hit that never became a placement because it was
filed as a collision: on this board a collision is usually two designators
claiming one label, and one of the two is right. R70 and R10 were read off the
same '4.7M' label and it is R70's; likewise C18 not C15, R30 not R20, R25 not
U1, R59 not R50, R60 not R66, R61 and R31 correct. The losing half of each
pair is placed here from its own label elsewhere.
J1 is printed twice on sheet 1, once at each end of the T1 primary; the left
one is recorded. U1 is printed only as the section label 'U1 A', which is what
the sheet gives.
Sheets 1 and 3 have no home for R10 and R57 respectively -- the reads dropped
there were the net labels 'HV LC1' and 'RST'. Both parts are placed on the
sheet that actually draws them.
Two markers already in the data were wrong and are corrected here. CR5's only
schematic position was sheet 2's CR9 label -- the 9-as-5 confusion, in the
agreed tier at 96% on nine votes -- so it is dropped there and placed on the
2A range bridge it actually labels on sheet 1. R8 had a correct sheet 1
position and a second one on sheet 2 sitting on R24's label; that one is
dropped and nothing replaces it, R8 is not on sheet 2.

_sheetsComment: Grid frames measured corner by corner on each sheet. They differ: the scan is
cropped inside the left zone band on sheets 1 and 3, and sheet 2 prints its row
letters on the left rather than the right, so no two sheets share a frame.
Sheet 4 is given none -- it carries the relay state table, not a circuit, and a
derived zone for a marker that does not exist would be worse than nothing.
_dropSchematicComment: Sheet 1's markers were reviewed one by one, and the failures are concentrated
in one place: the block of relay and transistor pinout legends along the bottom
of the sheet. 'K1, K2, K4, K8, K10, K11, K14' printed as a caption reads to the
reader exactly like eleven placements, and the FRONT/E-B-C pinouts do the same
for Q2 and Q3. Those parts are on the sheet -- their contacts are drawn in the
circuit -- but the marker landed on the caption, so it is dropped rather than
nudged, and the part is simply unplaced on that sheet. Same for TP2 to TP5,
which appear only in the sheet-1 legend box that lists all six test points and
the sheet each really lives on.
The rest are the ordinary schematic misreads: a value ('1.5M' as VR1, '196k' as
Z1), a net name ('-5 LH' as L1, 'I SNS' as Z1), a pin number, or a word of a
title block ('ABSOLUTE VALUE CIRCUIT' as L1, 'OUTPUT PEAK MEASURE' as MP1).
Sheet 3 fails the same way in its own idiom: it is the digital sheet, so the
reader finds capacitors in the 5801 drivers' output labels (C0, C1, C2, C3 are
net names there, not parts), test points in a 4051's I/O pin names (IO4, IO6),
and resistors in the port labels (PA2). Its relay coils and driver ICs, on the
Sheet 2's ambiguous and single tiers were reviewed the same way; its agreed tier
was sampled rather than swept -- see the coverage caveat in a14.reference.json.
_layersComment: Alignment of the photograph to board space. The high voltage shield (MP3) is
fitted in this photograph and covers the right-hand 40% of the board, so there
are no landmarks to be had out there and none of the four pairs below sits
further right than K7 at x=0.53. A homography fitted from one half of a board
extrapolates into the other half, so positions under the shield are a guess
drawn confidently -- which is why this is marked approximate and why the
coverage caveat says the photo tells you nothing on the right.
The pairs are silkscreen features rather than board corners: C27 and C2 across
the top, C11 and K7 across the bottom. Silkscreen is unambiguous in both images
in a way a corner under a bracket is not. Re-shoot with MP3 removed and the
same four still work, with room to add pairs on the right.
src is normalised in the drawing (5897 x 3351), dst in the photo (3400 x 2020).
